quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before riding, check your motorcycle throttle. It should:

options.text: Stay in place when you let go.
Stay loose when you let go.
Snap back when you let go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snap back when you let go.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your throttle and clutch. The throttle should snap back quickly when released, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: If you take a motorcycle turn too fast, what may happen?

options.text: Your ride will be more stable.
You may accidentally leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may accidentally leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to lose control. Your motorcycle may drift into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: The safest part of your lane:
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Places you next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position to avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire went flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle will jerk or sway. Stop riding and check your tires as soon as you notice this movement.

questions.question: When cars merge from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Never assume the drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Never assume drivers see you. Change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift, turn, and brake smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes because it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
Wear shorts if it is hot, for comfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright clothes when riding to help other drivers see you, even during daytime.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists is:
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet the most when riding. Boots should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger.
Are required for the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothes to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective clothing also helps.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than you normally would.
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. When carrying a passenger, reduce your speed, slow down earlier, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Should not be a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using the right braking technique is important for safe riding.

questions.question: What factors can affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect BAC: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket for motorcycle riding, what should you look for?
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket that covers your arms and fits snugly but allows free movement. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor give the best protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you be aware of?

options.text: Only what is in front of you
What is in front of and behind you

questions.correctAnswerText: What is in front of and behind you
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what is ahead of you. Also check your mirrors often to know what is behind you.

questions.question: Which colors should motorcycle riders wear for safety?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green. These colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: If there are hazards to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.
